title: Redwood Feb 2026 All-Hands
summary: Monthly company all-hands. Evelyn reviewed high-level metrics and strategic priorities for Q1, Samir provided an infra/incident update and roadmap for Dedicated and Private deployments, Lina covered product highlights including Optimize and rollout plans, and Maya shared GTM progress and upsell/expansion focus. Session ended with a live Q&A and a set of follow-ups (security docs, infra postmortem, hiring priorities).

transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-02-18
Time: 17:00 PST
Duration: ~75 minutes
Attendees: Evelyn Park (CEO), Samir Patel (CTO), Lina Gomez (VP Product), Rajiv Menon (Head of Eng), Maya Chen (Head of Sales), Oliver Reed (Head of Support), + all employees on call
Recording: Yes

Summary: See notes above; recording and slides to be shared.

00:00 - Evelyn: Hey everybody, thanks for joining today's all-hands, appreciate folks dialing in across timezones. Quick agenda - company metrics, infra update, product highlights, hiring, then Q&A. We'll keep this tight but leave lots of time for questions.

00:30 - Samir: I can kick off with infra - last week we had an incident on dedicated routing where a change in autoscaler logic caused a cascade and we lost ~30% of reserved throughput for an hour in us-west-2. Root cause appears to be an edge case with the burst policy applied to some pinned hosts, combined with a regression in the health-check backoff.

01:05 - Rajiv: to add, we rolled an emergency patch, mitigated within 40 minutes, and then a full fix later that night. Apologies to folks impacted. We're open-sourcing the postmortem internally and will publish the timeline.

01:40 - Speaker 1 (Evelyn?): Thank you, Rajiv. Can you also speak to customer impact and what we did for them?

02:00 - Samir: Yes - Maya's team did outreach for about 12 enterprise customers on Dedicated, provided credits and offered extra SRE support for the week. No data loss, this was capacity only, but for customers running latency-sensitive features it was noticeable. Root mitigations: change autoscaler to conservative backoff, add a safety cap on burst, and improve canary testing through the control plane.

02:40 - Lina: On product, big push for Optimize - the batching/caching recommender is in internal beta and early results show a 22% token-cost reduction for mid-size RLHF workloads, which is promising. We plan to start a limited pilot with 5 customers next month. Also, we're shipping function-calling extensions and structured output improvements in the API next sprint.

03:15 - Evelyn: Nice. Quick business metrics - revenue is tracking slightly above plan for Q1, churn is within expectations, but unit economics are still sensitive to heavy low-latency workloads. That's why Optimize and routing policies are priority one.

03:45 - Maya: From GTM, we've closed three mid-market deals for Dedicated in Feb and have four inbound trials for Private. We see two patterns driving expansion: regulated customers asking for VPC/on-prem, and platform teams wanting predictable SLOs and observability. Pricing conversations most often revolve around committed capacity vs burst pricing.

04:20 - Oliver: Support metrics - MTTR improved by 18% since December, but escalations around model fallbacks are up. We're building a standard fallback runbook for customers that pin to specific model versions and want graceful degradation.

05:00 - Employee Q (Sales): Quick question on SOC 2 - where are we in audits?

05:20 - Samir: We're halfway through the SOC 2 Type II audit period; external auditor visits completed in Jan. Expected report delivery in late March. We're also prepping ISO preliminary docs for customers asking about EU data residency.

06:00 - Employee Q (Eng): For the autoscaler fix, do we need any code freezes or special rollout windows?

06:20 - Rajiv: We'll do a staged rollout with canary to 10% of traffic, measure key metrics (latency p50/p95, RB cache hit rates) and if the canary is clean we'll expand. We will not do a global push during peak APAC hours.

07:00 - Lina: On roadmap - a few items: 1) Optimize recommender GA Q2, 2) Dedicated autoscaling ergonomics (policy templates) Q2, 3) Private deployment self-onboarding v0 late Q2, and 4) improved per-route tracing in Console for SLO debugging Q3.

07:50 - Evelyn: Hiring update - approved to add 12 roles this quarter across SRE, ML infra, and Sales Engineering. Hiring will prioritize SRE and two senior ML infra engineers to help with kernel selection & quantized runtime work. Managers will post job specs by end of week.

08:30 - Maya: On GTM motions, playbook for Dedicated renewals and expansion is being tested with two accounts. We also want to tighten the trial -> committed conversion funnel by improving onboarding docs and small benchmarking templates customers can run in their environment.

09:05 - Speaker 2 (Finance): Quick note on burn - runway unchanged but we are pacing non-essential spend until we hit Q2 efficiency targets. This affects discretionary hiring but core roles remain greenlighted.

09:35 - Q&A continues: employees ask about comms cadence for incidents, travel budgets, and global office plans. Answers: incident comms will get a triage note within 60 minutes and a full postmortem within 7 business days; travel budgets are still limited; EMEA hub plans remain in exploratory phase.

10:30 - Employee Q (Product): Any changes to pricing structure coming?

10:50 - Evelyn: No immediate changes; we'll test new unit incentives within a small cohort and present impact to leadership before broader changes. The focus is on improving unit economics with Optimize rather than raising list prices.

11:15 - Samir: One more technical note - we are rolling out improved KV cache observability to reduce cold-start penalties for long-chat sessions. This ties to Dedicated policy templates and should help latency-sensitive customers.

11:50 - Lina: We'll be sharing the detailed roadmap deck and an FAQ doc after the meeting. Please file product feedback in the #product-feedback channel so we can prioritize.

12:20 - Evelyn: Ok last things - thank you everyone, special thanks to the SRE team for the late-night fixes. Recap of action items: Samir postmortem, Lina roadmap deck, Maya GTM playbook, Oliver support runbook. Slides and recording will be shared.

12:50 - Q&A wrap and sign-off.

Note: Transcript contains a mix of speaker labels and occasional auto-generated mistakes (Speaker 1/2) and timestamps are approximate.
